paths.description: Homepage and movie-listing template; inspected desktop, mobile, preference variants, performance, privacy, accessibility, SSR and memory.
TV-show listing archetype; checked visual hierarchy and repeated premium promotion.
Movie-detail archetype and primary play action.
Primary viewing journey after following the detail page play link.
Authentication form archetype; inspected labels, validation wiring and autofill support.
Commercial membership choice surface; inspected pricing clarity.
Failure/recovery archetype using an unknown route.

findings.summary: The site does not respond to the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The default and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-identical (both 518,436 bytes), and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: There is no reduced-motion adaptation.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion CSS probe found no prefers-reduced-motion rule while the homepage uses carousel/transition UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduce branch that removes auto-advance and non-essential transitions.

findings.summary: The UI has no high-contrast or forced-colors adaptation.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found neither prefers-contrast nor forced-colors handling; Lighthouse also found 2.46:1 quality badges.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast styles and preserve visible control boundaries.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no view-transition rules or API styling across list-to-detail navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance list-to-detail navigation with same- or cross-document View Transitions and a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not react to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The long listing has static header chrome and the CSS probe found no scroll-state/query or scroll-progress implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky scroll-state-aware chrome or a progress/scrollability affordance on long listings.

findings.summary: Dropdown/overlay positioning is hand-built rather than anchored.
findings.evidence: The page contains category dropdowns and multiple custom overlays, while the CSS probe found no anchor-name or position-anchor rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for menus and contextual overlays.

findings.summary: Premium promotions repeatedly displace or obscure primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, shows and playback screenshots show a top banner plus large premium cards; on playback the membership panel covers most of the video area.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove on-load promotional overlays from the core journey; use one dismissible, non-modal promotion outside the content area.

findings.summary: Custom overlays do not use semantic dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The semantic probe found 0 dialog, 0 popover and 0 details elements despite three full-size fixed overlays; DOM shows custom modal divs.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with <dialog> and transient promotions with popover, including declarative light dismiss and focus management.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome dominates meaningful content.
findings.evidence: The shows screenshot gives most of the initial viewport to a premium card, and playback’s initial viewport is chiefly a membership upsell.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated promotional framing and keep titles, controls and content dominant in the first viewport.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: Mobile reflow succeeds, but the CSS probe found no @container/container-type use on reusable movie cards, banners or navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards and promotional modules while retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and some controls are too small.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on the first link computed outline:none and box-shadow:none; Lighthouse reports 32×32 carousel buttons without names.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide strong :focus-visible styling and enlarge controls to comfortable touch targets without hover-only behavior.

findings.summary: The primary watch journey does not reach a ready player in the observed state.
findings.evidence: After following the real /movies/play link and waiting seven seconds, the page still said “Loading … in 3s”; the video had readyState 0 and no currentSrc, while an upsell covered the player.
findings.suggestedFix: Load the playback source deterministically, expose retry/error states, and keep promotional UI out of the player startup path.

findings.summary: Playback loading state stalls without recovery.
findings.evidence: The seven-second playback capture remained on a three-second countdown with no visible retry, diagnostic or fallback action.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the countdown with truthful loading progress, timeout detection and explicit retry/back controls.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 7.1s, LCP 10.1s and TTI 10.1s (performance 0.55); a separate trace measured LCP 2.56s, showing material run-to-run variability.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, remove render-blocking work and defer non-critical third parties.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and third-party delivery delay content.
findings.evidence: HAR found four parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets; Lighthouse estimates 1,930ms render-blocking savings and flags font-display/network dependency issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline critical CSS, defer non-critical CSS, self-host/subset fonts and keep async third-party scripts out of the critical path.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 317 KiB unused JavaScript and 70 KiB unused CSS; HAR transfers 676 KiB script for the listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by route and conditionally load reCAPTCHA, analytics and playback-only code when needed.

findings.summary: Several interactive controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found unnamed carousel buttons and search links; the filter form’s select controls have no associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon controls explicit accessible names and associate visible labels with every form control.

findings.summary: Quality badges fail minimum text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2.46:1 white-on-#79b617 contrast for FHD/HD badges, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the badge color or change foreground color to meet WCAG contrast.

findings.summary: Heading, landmark and focus structure is broken.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found invalid heading order, no main landmark and presentation-role conflicts; the focus probe showed no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one <main>, use sequential headings, remove conflicting presentational roles and implement :focus-visible.

findings.summary: Some touch targets remain undersized despite successful mobile reflow.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout has no horizontal overflow, but Lighthouse reports 32×32 carousel controls, below a comfortable target size.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes to at least 44×44 CSS pixels while preserving the successful reflow.

findings.summary: Images do not reserve layout space or consistently use responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all 100 images missing width/height attributes, 34 missing srcset and 66 legacy-format assets; Lighthouse also flags unsized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and responsive srcset/sizes; modernise appropriate assets.

findings.summary: The page triggers poor platform hygiene signals on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a notification permission request on startup, three BFCache failure reasons and DevTools Inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Never request permission on load; request it after a clear user gesture and resolve BFCache/Inspector blockers.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable or meaningfully named.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors; DOM includes href="#" action links and unnamed links, though viewport and robots are valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions and real destination hrefs with descriptive text for navigation.

findings.summary: Movie detail pages omit structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The detail page has accurate title, description, canonical and Open Graph data, but the probe found no JSON-LD for the visible movie entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add schema.org Movie JSON-LD matching the title, year, description, image and rating shown on-page.

findings.summary: Session and analytics cookies are not marked Secure and baseline security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The cookie audit found all four first-party cookies without Secure, including PHPSESSID with SameSite=None; headers found no CSP, HSTS or nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure and appropriate SameSite on every cookie; deploy HSTS, CSP and nosniff over HTTPS.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party code load before consent or need.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 9 third-party origins and Google Analytics/Tag Manager; HAR attributes 692 KiB and 19 requests to third parties, while Lighthouse found three third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors, gate analytics on consent, and conditionally load reCAPTCHA only where a protected form is used.

findings.summary: Permissions are requested out of context and sign-in lacks modern assistance.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse detected a notification permission request on page load; login uses password-only fields without autocomplete tokens and no observed WebAuthn/passkey affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Request notifications only after user intent; add autocomplete=username/current-password and offer passkey sign-in.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are comprehensively missing.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to missing CSP/HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for the script-heavy app.

findings.summary: The document declares language but not direction and shows no translation-ready strategy.
findings.evidence: DOM reports html lang="en-US" but no dir attribute; the fixed English UI and physical-position-heavy custom layout provide no evidence of bidi readiness.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir explicitly or derive it from locale and migrate layout rules to logical properties.

findings.summary: Repeated premium nagging pressures users throughout the free core flow.
findings.evidence: Premium prompts appear on the homepage, shows listing, detail and playback pages; playback places the upsell directly over the promised viewing area.
findings.suggestedFix: Limit promotion frequency, persist dismissal, and keep the free path equally clear without obstruction.

findings.summary: The login form omits autofill tokens.
findings.evidence: Both email and password inputs have labels but autocomplete is absent, preventing reliable username/current-password assistance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email plus autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password; retain labels and appropriate input modes.

findings.summary: Asset delivery wastes bytes through non-responsive and legacy images.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 34 images without srcset and 66 legacy-format assets; Lighthouse estimates 251 KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide responsive srcset/sizes and AVIF/WebP where appropriate, while reserving dimensions.

findings.summary: Heavy third-party work runs on a listing before it is needed.
findings.evidence: The homepage loads 383 KiB reCAPTCHA runtime, 167 KiB Tag Manager and nine third-party origins although no protected form is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay reCAPTCHA until a protected form opens and reduce or batch analytics work.

findings.summary: Third parties consume a disproportionate share of the initial page budget.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 692,131 third-party bytes out of 1,602,375 transferred bytes (43%) across 19 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, self-host essential fonts and remove low-value vendors.

findings.summary: The content is crawlable but exposes no structured agent capability.
findings.evidence: Discoverability is excellent (100% raw-HTML coverage), but no WebMCP/agentic tool or structured action interface was observed for search/watch-list tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider a read-only search/discovery WebMCP tool with explicit confirmation for account-changing actions.
